angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 786,141 km at 68.23 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 14.6568 +/- 0.0160 mas (same row, RUWE 0.94): 68.23 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.13 solar radii from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-128.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract): 786,141 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.851969 solar masses from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-128.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6086 K from Hord et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-128.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hord et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-128.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-128.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.262, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 36481: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-128 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.18874, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 4621607053580909568, flags_flame 00: age_flame 4.80733 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 3.9731648 to 5.6410327)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
